name: io.github.your-org/mcp-template
description: Template MCP server: profiles, a response budget, self-serving docs and skills, stdio and HTTP

environmentVariables.name: MCP_PROFILE
environmentVariables.description: Which tools are listed and callable: core (the smallest set that can read and change something, for small local models), readonly (never writes), or all. A tool outside the profile cannot be called.

environmentVariables.name: MCP_MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES
environmentVariables.description: Ceiling on one tool answer, in bytes; 0 removes it. Defaults to the profile's: core 24000, readonly 32000, all none. An answer over it is replaced by valid JSON naming the next step.

environmentVariables.name: MCP_GATE
environmentVariables.description: Set to off to skip asking the backend which optional features it supports. With it on, tools the backend cannot serve are withheld from tools/list.

environmentVariables.name: MCP_TRANSPORT
environmentVariables.description: stdio (the default) for one client that starts this process, or http to serve Streamable HTTP at /mcp for many, each with its own bearer token.

environmentVariables.name: MCP_HTTP_PORT
environmentVariables.description: Port to listen on in HTTP mode.

environmentVariables.name: MCP_HTTP_HOST
environmentVariables.description: Address to bind in HTTP mode. Use 127.0.0.1 to serve this machine only.

environmentVariables.name: MCP_HTTP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS
environmentVariables.description: Browser origins allowed to call /mcp in HTTP mode, comma-separated; * allows any. Empty serves none. MCP clients that are not web pages send no Origin and are unaffected.

environmentVariables.name: MCP_HTTP_ALLOWED_HOSTS
environmentVariables.description: Host header values answered to in HTTP mode, comma-separated. Empty accepts any; set it to the published name as a DNS-rebinding guard.

environmentVariables.name: MCP_HTTP_RATE_LIMIT
environmentVariables.description: Requests per minute per session in HTTP mode, as a token bucket. 0 turns it off.

environmentVariables.name: EXAMPLE_ACCEPTED_TOKENS
environmentVariables.description: Example backend only: the bearer tokens HTTP callers may present, comma-separated. Unset, HTTP mode accepts nobody. Replace with your backend's own credential handling.
